You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The data points to mid-2018, most likely June 2018.

- **Labor market:** unemployment is 3.9%, which matches April–June 2018 (3.9% in April, 3.8% in May, 4.0% in June).
- **Rates:** the fed funds rate is 1.92%, which matches April–June 2018 (1.82% in April, 1.91% in May, 1.92% in June). The Fed hiked in June 2018.
- **Yields:** the 2-year yield is 2.64% and the 10-year is 2.86%, with a spread of 0.22. In May 2018 the 10-year closed near 2.83% and the 2-year near 2.5%. In June 2018 the 10-year was about 2.85% and the 2-year about 2.52%.
- **Inflation:** headline CPI of 2.89% fits May 2018 (2.8%) or June 2018 (2.9%). Core CPI of 2.33% looks like May–June 2018 (2.2% in May, 2.3% in June).
- **Dollar and EM:** the dollar is up sharply over 3 months (+5.02), emerging-market equity is down 7.2% over 3 months, and gold is down 7.2% over 3 months. All of this fits the spring 2018 dollar rally.
- **Equities:** US large-cap equity is up 2.8% over the month, which fits June 2018 (S&P 500 up about 0.6%) less well and May 2018 (up about 2.4%) better.

The 10-year yield was about 2.86% at the end of May 2018 and the 2-year was about 2.4%, which would give a spread near 0.45. The supplied spread of 0.22 therefore fits June better, though the 2-year in June was around 2.52%. The 1-month Treasury returns are positive, which fits May, when yields fell from 3.0% to 2.86%, but that conflicts with the spread. I weigh the policy rate and spread toward June and the equity and Treasury returns toward May, so I pick June with May as the alternative.
